To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcriptional factor AP-1 is present at low levels in undifferentiated F9 cells and that its activity is stimulated by a protein that binds c-fos but not c-june.
the c-fos protein is required for activation of a DNA binding transcriptional activity that is associated with cellular differentiation.

(1) c-fos is involved in the regulation of AP-1 activity during cellular differentiation; (2) c-fos can activate AP-1 activity in vitro; (3) c-fos protein is present in EC cell extracts; and (4) AP-1 activity is present in undifferentiated EC cells
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of transcription factors involved in differentiation.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate gene expression during differentiation and development.
the identification of the proteins responsible for activation of AP-1 binding in EC cell extracts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-fos is required for activation of AP-1 in F9 cells.
the c-fos protein is the protein that stimulates the DNA binding activity of a transcriptional factor in undifferentiated EC cells.
c-fos protein can be detected in undifferentiated embryonal carcinoma cells, and its expression is stimulated by retinoic and cyclic AMP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
c-fos protein can be activated by a protein kinase cascade, and this activation is required for its ability to stimulate AP-1 transcriptional activity.
c-fos is a transcriptional regulator that is involved in the regulation of differentiation in undifferentiated embryonal carcinoma cells.
the c-fos protein, in conjunction with other factors, is able to activate a DNA binding transcriptional complex in EC cells.
